_doc: OSCAR Figure 4 (RIGHT), Qwen3-8B column: job-level throughput at a fixed 100k
input as a function of batch size, with prefix warm-up.
Paper OSCAR speedup vs BF16: 2.88 / 3.35 / 3.44 at BS=1 / 8 / 32.
Paper Saw-INT4: 1.52 / 2.32 / 2.09 -- not implemented here, series absent.
The shared prefix is what makes BS=32 at 100k feasible: 32 x 100k = 3.2M
tokens exceeds the pool, but one shared prefix costs ~100k plus short tails.

chunked-prefill-size 102400 (> the 100k prefix) is REQUIRED: the mixed-KV pool only commits the first prefill chunk to the radix cache, so at the sglang default of 8192 a 100k prefix caches only 7936 tokens and the paper's full-prefix-cache-hit protocol silently degrades into a re-prefill. Verified: with 102400 a repeat 100k request reports #cached-token: 99728 and TTFT drops 6814ms -> 263ms. This is a documented DEVIATION -- the paper does not override this flag. Pool is capped at 1.2M for quant arms to leave room for the large chunk; bf16 keeps auto (~374k) since 1.2M BF16 tokens would need ~173GB.
